Swiss Equity Strategy Comparison

Executive Summary

We tested 10 Swiss equity strategy candidates against the Swiss Performance Index (SPI). Each notebook applies investability controls, simulates net returns with 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction cost, and reports SPI-relative performance.

Best annual return
S4 8.73%
Best Sharpe, rf=0
S14 0.67
Lowest annual volatility
S14 10.24%
Current interpretation: S4 has the highest annual return, while S14 has the highest Sharpe and S3 is close behind but with high turnover. S7 looks like the most balanced factor candidate. S8 is useful as a small-cap quality sleeve. S14 and S22 are defensive overlays rather than return-maximizing stock-selection strategies.

Backtest Design

Universe and data. The strategies use the Swiss equity market data provided in market_data.parquet, jkp_data.parquet, and spi_index.csv. SPI is used as the benchmark.

Bias controls. Fundamental data is lagged by 90 days where accounting variables are used. Selection uses data available at or before each rebalance date. Market timing overlays use monthly SPI signals based only on past index levels.

Costs. Net returns include 1% annual fixed cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost. S8 additionally reports a higher small-cap cost sensitivity. S14 and S22 charge both base-portfolio trading costs and exposure-change costs.

Portfolio construction. The strategies use either constrained minimum variance, capped inverse-volatility weights, or an exposure overlay on top of a liquid inverse-volatility base portfolio.

Strategy Sections

S1: Defensive Quality Compounder

source notebook

Targets firms with positive profitability, acceptable leverage, lower realized volatility, and quality characteristics. Designed to compete with SPI through lower downside risk rather than aggressive alpha.

Implementation

  • Selection: Return-history, trading-gap, liquidity, lagged fundamentals, positive profitability, leverage cap, volatility cap, and quality floor.
  • Construction: Long-only minimum-variance portfolio with stock and sector concentration controls.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.

Snapshot

Annualized return7.51%
Annualized volatility14.74%
Sharpe, rf=00.57
Average holdings20.8
Average turnover42.3%

Main risk: Can lag in strong risk-on markets because the screen and optimizer are deliberately defensive.

S2: Low-Volatility Minimum-Variance Core

source notebook

Keeps the lower-volatility part of the liquid Swiss equity universe and lets the optimizer build the most defensive basket inside that universe.

Implementation

  • Selection: Return-history, trading-gap, liquidity, and low realized-volatility screen.
  • Construction: Long-only minimum-variance portfolio with max stock and sector caps.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.

Snapshot

Annualized return6.60%
Annualized volatility10.99%
Sharpe, rf=00.64
Average holdings34.6
Average turnover26.9%

Main risk: Lower volatility comes with lower expected upside during broad equity rallies.

S3: Momentum with Crash Control

source notebook

Captures medium-term winner continuation while avoiding the most fragile high-volatility and high-beta momentum names.

Implementation

  • Selection: Return-history, trading-gap, liquidity, composite momentum score, volatility cap, and beta cap against SPI.
  • Construction: Capped inverse-volatility weights.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.

S5: Value Trap Avoidance

source notebook

source notebook

S7: Conservative Investment / Profitability

source notebook

Favors firms with strong operating profitability and controlled investment growth, based on the idea that conservative capital allocators compound better.

Implementation

  • Selection: Return-history, liquidity, lagged profitability, asset/investment growth, leverage, quality, and volatility screens.
  • Construction: Capped inverse-volatility weights tilted toward a profitability-investment score.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.

S8: Swiss Small-Cap Quality

source notebook

Targets smaller Swiss names only when liquidity and financial quality are acceptable.

Implementation

  • Selection: Excludes the largest market-cap stocks, then applies liquidity, return-history, profitability, quality, and volatility controls.
  • Construction: Capped inverse-volatility weights with a stricter max stock weight and separate high-cost sensitivity.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.
  • High-cost sensitivity: daily mean 0.000313 after 0.5% transaction cost.

S14: Trend-Following Equity Exposure

source notebook

Keeps a liquid Swiss equity base portfolio but reduces total equity exposure when SPI trades below a 10-month moving average.

Implementation

  • Selection: Broad liquid base universe with return-history, trading-gap, liquidity, and volatility controls.
  • Construction: Base inverse-volatility portfolio. Equity exposure is 100% above trend and 50% below trend, with exposure-change costs.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.
  • Average equity exposure: 0.843; exposure changes: 43; average overlay cost/day: 6.7e-05.

Snapshot

Annualized return6.55%
Annualized volatility10.24%
Sharpe, rf=00.67
Average holdings79.9
Average turnover17.6%

Main risk: Trend rules reduce drawdowns but can underperform in sideways markets due to whipsaw.

S22: Drawdown-Controlled Portfolio

source notebook

Uses SPI drawdown as a risk-control signal and reduces equity exposure after pre-defined loss thresholds.

Implementation

  • Selection: Broad liquid base universe with return-history, trading-gap, liquidity, and volatility controls.
  • Construction: Base inverse-volatility portfolio. Equity exposure is 100%, 70%, or 50% depending on SPI drawdown thresholds.
  • Costs: 1% fixed annual cost and 0.2% transaction/rebalancing cost are included in net returns.
  • Average equity exposure: 0.786; exposure changes: 30; average overlay cost/day: 6.2e-05.
